correctness.rationale: The exact SO(3) Haar class integral and spin character identity reduce positivity to consecutive cosine-moment differences. The \(\alpha=2\) closed form has strict positivity from monotonicity of \( (x-\sin x)/x^3 \) for all \(x>0\). A correctly normalized positive beta mixture extends all coefficients to every \(\alpha>2\). The endpoint Fourier expansion at the cutoff has a nonzero leading sine term of order \(\ell^{-\alpha-1}\), dominating the smooth \(O(\ell^{-3})\) contribution for \(0<\alpha<2\). Periodic and equidistributed phases yield infinitely many negative spectral blocks for every support radius; Peter-Weyl completeness proves strict positive definiteness in the permitted regime. The bundled finite checker passed 374 consistency checks but is not asserted to prove the infinite statements.

The distinct result is necessity for every radius plus negative-spin oscillatory asymptotics for all \(0<\alpha<2\). A focused statement-and-implication comparison of Xu Theorem 2.4, Lu 2025, spherical Polya criteria, generic projective characterization and related fixed-exponent SO3 work did not identify the necessary classification; incomplete source coverage leaves an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: A structurally natural family of compactly supported central covariance kernels has a known sufficiency threshold but no necessity from those results. The all-aperture if-and-only-if classification and infinitely many explicit spectral obstructions resolve that motivated gap; high-frequency sign density explains why finitely many positive checks are misleading. The result applies uniformly over real support radii and exponents, with an exact endpoint. It is not a routine computation of a tabulated example.
